text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran the SLA-oriented bench on the new admission flow and hit a few weird regressions on long-prefix workloads.
igor: Ugh. Which bench and what's the regression magnitude?
maya: It's the smokefast sampler against golden inputs. 95th p50->p95 tail widened ~30ms on A100 test pool. Not huge but violates our canary SLA.
sam: Can you paste the run id? and the exact config?
maya: run id: `bench-5078-gold-v2`
config: `seq_len_histogram=heavy-left, batching=auto, kv_cache=enabled, quant=fp16`
Also saw occasional tokenizer alignment errors in the logs (token mismatch with reference).
leila: Tokenizer mismatch is worrisome — could be an ingest descriptor change or a tokenizer binary mismatch. Did the model descriptor include `tokenizer_version`?
maya: Yes, descriptor had `tokenizer_version: bert-v3` but the golden artifact used `bert-v2` during earlier bench generation.
taylor: That explains drift. If golden inputs were tokenized differently, latency calc + prefix lengths shift. We need stronger handshake validation between intake and goldset generation.
igor: Agreed. Two things: 1) prevent goldsets being generated with implicit tokenizer defaults, 2) add a pre-bench verifier that re-tokenizes golden inputs with model descriptor and asserts identical token lengths.
sam: For the pre-bench verifier, do we fail the admission or just mark flaky? We need to balance onboarding throughput.
leila: Fail fast for mismatched tokenizer version — that's a correctness problem. For small token deltas (<=1 token) maybe mark as warning and schedule deep bench.
aylor: +1 on two-tier policy. Also propose we capture `prefix_token_distribution` in the artifact metadata so bench runner can simulate batching better.
maya: I like that. It'd help the runtime pick kernel configs during onboarding.
ken: Related: the smokefast sampler currently uses single-run p95 as canary — that amplifies noise. We should use bootstrap sampling across N shards and compute median-of-means.
igor: Good point, ken. Median-of-means reduces false positives. Set N=5 with min 50 samples each?
ken: Sounds reasonable. We'll need to update the bench runner to support multi-shard aggregation.
sam: Implementation note: keep the single-run flag for manual runs. Automatic admission should use aggregated metric.
leila: Also we should wire the `tokenizer_checksum` into the admission handshake so runtime refuses to serve if runtime tokenizer != descriptor checksum.
maya: For the compatibility side, I also saw a case where quantized kernels caused slight probability mass shifts leading to rerank instability. Not a perf issue but quality.
taylor: Can we add a lightweight perplexity/regression eval on a small probe set during admit? If quality delta > threshold we block.
igor: Yes — a quick bleu/perplexity surrogate across 200 probes is cheap and catches big shifts. Keep thresholds conservative for new model archetypes.
ken: Ops question: where do these validators live? In the intake service or in a separate bench orchestrator?
sam: Architecture: intake vetting should do descriptor & artifact sanity + tokenizer checks. Bench/quality runs live in bench orchestrator with an admission API that returns pass/warn/fail and telemetry.
leila: Make sure telemetry includes `run_seed`, `node_pool_id`, `kernel_variant`, and `batch_config` so we can reproduce.
maya: Also include `goldset_artifact_id` and `goldset_tokenizer_v` in telemetry.
igor: Agreed. One more tradeoff: tighter admission rules slow onboarding. We should make a policy that auto-approves dev-tier models with warnings but blocks enterprise-tier.
ken: Could we do a staged approval: dev->shadow->live. Shadow runs route traffic to older variant while verifying metrics.
taylor: That's our canary flow already for runtime, but we need same in onboarding: shadow-serving smoke for 24h before live for important customers.
sam: Action items: 1) ken/igor update bench-runner for aggregated p95 and multi-shard median-of-means (ken), 2) leila/maya add tokenizer checksum and pre-bench verifier (leila), 3) sam/taylor design staged admission policy + telemetry fields (sam).
leila: I'll open a tiny RFC for the tokenizer checksum handshake and add the descriptor field.
ken: I'll PR the bench-runner change with tests.
igor: I'll mock a failure mode to ensure we don't block too many models in prod.
maya: Thanks all — ping me if you need the failing run logs. I attached the `bench-5078-gold-v2` log zip to the thread in case you want it.
dev-bot: File uploaded: bench-5078-gold-v2-logs.zip
sam: Great. Let's sync after the PRs land.
leila: ETA for RFC: EOD Friday.
ken: PR by mid-next-week.
igor: Will run simulated admission on a sample of 50 models after PR.
maya: Cool. If nothing else, this will reduce noisy canary alerts. :thumbsup:
